clue.text: Wimbledon champion describes time in prison

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so one word is drawn around another here

blocks.note: Carlos Alcaraz, Spanish tennis player who won Wimbledon in 2023 and 2024
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A tennis star's biography covers a spell behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describes' reads as 'tells of', but here it means 'goes around', as a compass describes a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcatraz was the notorious federal penitentiary on an island in San Francisco Bay, so the name stands for a prison.

clue.text: SPFL club right to back revolting supporter over swear-word

indicators.note: to revolt is to turn over, so the word for the support garment is turned round
in a down entry, putting one piece to the back of another places it after the first

blocks.note: a bra is an undergarment that gives support
R is the usual abbreviation for right
an oath can be a curse or profanity

explanation.surface: A football club backs a rebellious fan who has been caught swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' says the first group of letters sits above the last word in this down entry. The SPFL is the Scottish Professional Football League.
explanation.definitionFit: Arbroath FC is a Scottish football club from the Angus coastal town, playing in the professional league.

clue.text: Mark, when writing, detailed dependency

indicators.note: read as de-tailed, meaning the word loses its tail, its final letter

blocks.note: a dependency is a territory ruled by another country

explanation.surface: A writer's note about a thoroughly described addiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' looks like 'thorough', but it is split as de-tailed: the last letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A colon is a punctuation mark used in written text, two dots one above the other.

clue.text: Article about inspiring location essentially for entertainment venue

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letters are kept
to inspire is to breathe in, so the outer letters take in other letters

blocks.note: the definite article
re means concerning or about
the two central letters of the word location

explanation.surface: Something about a key spot serves as the setting for a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article about' together makes a single shell, and the middle letters go inside it, between the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is a building where plays and shows are staged for an audience.

clue.text: About to tuck into second tart

indicators.note: something tucked into another is placed inside it

blocks.note: to second someone is to back or help them, and aid is help
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone is just about to dig into a second pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' looks like a pastry, but it means sour. 'Second' is a verb meaning to support.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid as an adjective describes a sharp, sour taste, which is what tart means.

clue.text: Thrill going around capital city, Rabat, on vacation

indicators.note: a vacated word is emptied, leaving only its first and last letters
going around means turning back the other way, so the combined letters are read from the end

blocks.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
the first and last letters of Rabat

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker gets a buzz touring capitals like Rabat.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are joined and then the whole is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a quiver or shiver of feeling, just as a thrill is a sudden quivering sensation.

clue.text: Pragmatic type of A-lister diversified

indicators.note: something diversified has been varied and made different, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, without the hyphen

explanation.surface: A celebrity who has branched out is a practical sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist is a person who deals with things as they actually are, which describes a pragmatic person.

clue.text: Chap receiving bill works for PM

indicators.note: one who receives takes something in, so the word holds the others inside it

blocks.note: a chap is a man
AC is short for account, a bill
a mill is a factory or works

explanation.surface: A man handed an invoice is working for the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill and works go in together as one inserted chunk. Harold Macmillan was British Prime Minister from 1957 to 1963.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Macmillan was a Conservative British Prime Minister, so the surname answers the abbreviation for that office.

clue.text: Thinking highly of sailor

blocks.note: first meaning: holding someone in high esteem
second meaning: a non-commissioned seaman in the navy

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests admiring a seaman; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate someone is to esteem them, and in the Royal Navy a rating is an ordinary seaman.

clue.text: Pavlova maybe ran, liable to need whisking

indicators.note: whisking stirs things up, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pavlova dessert recipe in which the ingredients will need whisking.
explanation.walkthrough: Pavlova and whisking point to the meringue dessert, but the definition is Anna Pavlova, the Russian dancer it was named after.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna Pavlova was a celebrated Russian prima ballerina, so she is an example of a ballet dancer.

clue.text: House and car barely guarded

indicators.note: something bare is stripped, so the word loses its outer letters

blocks.note: Audi is a German car make
fenced in means protected or guarded

explanation.surface: A home and vehicle are only lightly protected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' looks like a home, but in the theatre the house is the people watching.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre, the house means the people in the seats, which is another word for the spectators.

clue.text: Royal occasion, one north of the Border?

blocks.note: a means one
someone living north of the English border is a Scot

explanation.surface: Is a royal event something for a Scot from across the Border to attend?
explanation.walkthrough: The Border is the boundary between England and Scotland. Royal Ascot is the June horse-race meeting attended by the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Ascot is an annual horse-racing meeting in Berkshire with royal patronage, a major society event.

clue.text: Soldiers in battle, regularly decorated

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is taken

blocks.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Troops in combat were routinely given medals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link putting soldiers inside battle, but it belongs to the letters being picked.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately adorned, which is what heavily decorated describes.

clue.text: Supplement habit, not cheap initially

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word before it
not tells us that a letter must be removed from the larger word

blocks.note: a habit can mean a drug dependency
the first letter of cheap

explanation.surface: A costly vitamin-taking routine that doesn't come cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: An addition is something added on, as is a supplement.

clue.text: Dieter watches them, Erica and Sol performing

indicators.note: performers move around, so these letters are put into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone on a diet watches two performers, Erica and Sol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watches' looks like a verb of viewing a show, but it means keeps count of.
explanation.definitionFit: People trying to lose weight count the energy units in their food, so they monitor these.

clue.text: Volatile paint? Ridiculous!

blocks.note: tempera is a paint made with egg yolk
mental is slang for crazy or ridiculous

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a volatile paint is absurd.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone temperamental has unpredictable moods, which is what volatile means of a person.

clue.text: Wicked crime Stan cracked

definitions.note: miscreant is chiefly a noun, but has an older adjective sense meaning villainous

indicators.note: something cracked is broken up, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nasty offence that Stan pulled off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked' reads as solved, as in cracking a case, but it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, miscreant means villainous or depraved, a close match for wicked.

clue.text: Time spent inside gallery ultimately flexible

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: a stretch is slang for a prison sentence
the final letter of gallery

explanation.surface: A prisoner's sentence served in an art gallery proves adaptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' is slang for in prison, so the whole phrase is one prison term, not an insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stretchy can be pulled out of shape and spring back, so it is elastic or flexible.

clue.text: Leading opposition MPs in dance show, a bit unusual

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary, so the letters are put in an irregular order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Senior opposition politicians appearing on a dance show is rather odd.
explanation.walkthrough: In UK politics the main opposition party names MPs to mirror each government minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shadow Cabinet is the group of senior opposition party MPs each assigned to monitor a government department.

clue.text: Assistant giving rise to some notoriety locally?

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words, so the letters lie within them
in a down entry, rising means reading upwards, from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: the letters running across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A helper gains a bit of local fame.
explanation.walkthrough: The run of letters straddles the join of the two words and is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte is an attendant who assists a priest in church services, so a helper or follower.

clue.text: Number supporting award for composer

indicators.note: in a down entry, a supporting piece holds up the other from beneath, so it comes second

blocks.note: a Brit is one of the annual British music industry awards
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A song backs up a music award for a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Number reads as a song, but it is the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten was a twentieth-century English composer, of Peter Grimes among other works.

clue.text: United, meeting Palace, primarily go to get result

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: U is the abbreviation for United in team names
the first letter of Palace
a go or attempt is a shot

explanation.surface: A football fixture: United meet Crystal Palace and attack for a result.
explanation.walkthrough: United and Palace look like football clubs, as in Manchester United and Crystal Palace, but give single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot is the final outcome or consequence of something, so it means the result.

clue.text: Occasional table?

blocks.note: surface reading: a small side table used now and then
setter's reading: a word meaning occasional that also names the chemist's chart of elements

explanation.walkthrough: An occasional table is a piece of furniture; the question mark warns the answer is a synonym of occasional that also precedes the word table in chemistry.
explanation.definitionFit: Periodic means happening at intervals, and the periodic table is Mendeleev's chart of the chemical elements.

clue.text: Trustworthy engineers departing, it's likely

indicators.note: departing means leaving, so those letters go out of the word

blocks.note: trustworthy means dependable
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Reliable engineers are leaving, it seems probable.
explanation.definitionFit: Liable to do something means apt or likely to do it.

clue.text: Close to villa slice up wood

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its last letter is kept
in a down entry, going up means the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the last letter of villa
a slab is a thick slice

explanation.surface: Near a country house, someone chops timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to villa' reads as 'near the villa', but it means the villa's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light tropical wood, used for model making.

clue.text: Reportedly animal fodder running out perhaps in ring

indicators.note: reportedly means as said, so the answer is how the words are spoken

blocks.note: hay is dried grass fed to livestock
supplies running out are getting low

explanation.surface: A report that cattle feed is running short around the paddock.
explanation.walkthrough: The two spoken words run together say the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A halo is a circle of light, such as around a saint's head or the moon, so a ring.

clue.text: Villain in possession of diamonds, not very exciting?

indicators.note: taking possession of new letters while giving one up means a swap of one letter for another
not marks the letter that is given up in the exchange

blocks.note: a heavy is the villain in a film or play
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A jewel thief holding diamonds, but is it really thrilling?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not very' reads as 'hardly', but very is the letter that goes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Heady means intoxicating or thrilling, which is close to exciting; the question mark marks the loose fit.

clue.text: Clever clogs with studies over penning story

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for studying is read backwards
to pen is to enclose, as in a sheep pen, so one word holds another

blocks.note: crams means studies hard for an exam
a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A know-it-all who has done their studies and writes a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' reads as writing, fitting the story, but it means enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is a know-it-all; clever clogs is the British informal term for the same show-off.

clue.text: Noble deed by daughter

blocks.note: a title deed proves ownership of property, so title can mean a deed
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: An aristocrat's act benefits their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: A titled person holds a rank such as lord or duchess, so belongs to the aristocracy.

clue.text: Four, say, in spring fairly absent at intervals

indicators.note: letters missing at regular intervals leave every second one, so alternate letters are kept

blocks.note: a bound is a leap or spring
the second, fourth and sixth letters of fairly

explanation.surface: Four, perhaps, in a season of mostly missing days.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a four is a ball hit across the edge of the field, scoring four runs. 'Spring' looks like the season but means a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a boundary is a shot reaching the edge of the field, and a four is one example.
